name: cave stalactites r11 A1
label: theme-cave-stal-r11-A1
reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (1/4)

answer.evidence: Three stalactites hang from a ceiling strip at rows 0-1, which is a 1-2 row band that reads as an outline or attachment strip and has no front-edge line or eave shadow. Below it, each cone narrows steadily from about 31px wide at row 3 to 2px at row 29. The shading is a light left side and a dark right side, with no horizontal surface, no ellipse and no contents. The whole piece is a vertical face drawn in elevation, which is acceptable for a flat wall-mounted object but has no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows three grey-brown stalactites with about 4 visible value steps each: a light left edge, a mid body, a dark right side and a deep tip. There are only 7 raw colours in total and 6 visible tones per tile, against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, and a few craggy highlight dots and facet breaks give some texture. 76% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline leans toward grey-black and only partly takes the tone of the rock, whereas Beodeul uses tinted material-tone edges (hedge 0%, stall 1%). The shapes are repeated near-identical cones with little per-rock shading, grain or clustering, and they look thinner and more sticker-like than the well and stall. The candidate is a clean, usable piece but sits below the references on shading depth, texture and outline craft.

surfaces.part: light band at the root of each cone

answer.evidence: Three tapering cones hang from a dark ceiling strip at row 0. The only top-like area is a 2-row lighter band at rows 1-2 where each cone meets the ceiling. It has no front-edge line and no eave shadow below it, so it counts as a rim or highlight, not a horizontal surface. Below it the cones taper in width from about 31 px to 4 px by row 25 and end in a point at row 29. They are drawn as a flat front-facing elevation with a light side and a dark shadow side, and no ellipse, roof or visible contents. As a wall-mounted or hanging piece it is plausibly a flat object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows three grey-brown stalactites with 6 visible tones per tile and 0% near-flat coverage. That is below the well (20), the stall (17) and the hedge (9). Shading is roughly 4 steps (light face, mid, dark side, deep tip), against about 5-6 on the reference materials. Edge pixels are 76% near-neutral, so the outline leans toward a dark grey line rather than a tinted dark material tone, though some brown lean remains, hence 'mixed'. The ridges have a little vertical grain, but the faces are mostly smooth, with no per-stone speckle or clump variation like the hedge leaves or well stones. The silhouettes are clean but sticker-like, thinner and simpler than the best references. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: stalactite cluster (three hanging cones) with a ceiling strip at the top

answer.evidence: Three stalactite cones hang from a ceiling strip (rows 0-1, width 48). They are drawn as flat, shaded vertical shapes tapering to a point (width 32 down to 2). No horizontal top surface appears: there is no ellipse, no front-edge line with eave shadow, and no roof plane. The lighter rows 1-2 at the cone tops are a highlight where the stalactites meet the ceiling, not a top surface. The object is a flat wall-mounted piece, so a front elevation is the normal reading.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is three grey-brown stalactites with a clear light-to-dark ramp of about 4 steps, plus a few ridge and crack dots. It has no flat 5x5 areas (0% near-flat). It shows 6 visible tones per tile, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the well. That is lower than the richer references, though the bench and lamp are too thin to measure. 76% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline leans grey-black rather than a clearly tinted dark material tone, which I call mixed. The shapes are fairly simple and uniform, with limited per-rock shading or clumping, and the three forms look somewhat sticker-like next to the well and stall. Overall it is thinner than the best references, with only 7 raw colours in total against 38-40 for the stall and well. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: three hanging stalactite cones, drawn as one cluster
light band at the cave-ceiling attachment of each cone

answer.evidence: The three stalactites are tapering cones seen face-on. Width goes from 48 at rows 0-1 down to 2 at row 29. Rows 1-2 are a lighter band where each cone meets the ceiling, but it has no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse width profile. It is a highlight on a vertical face, not a horizontal surface. The cones are shaded left-to-right, light to dark, as a vertical face would be. No receding side face is drawn. This is a flat wall-mounted elevation, and a stalactite hanging from a ceiling would not be expected to show a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is three grey-brown stalactite cones with about 4 visible lightness steps (light left face, mid, dark right side, deep shadow) and only 7 raw colours. It has 6 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the well, so it is clearly below the richer references. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, but the texture is only a few streak dots down each cone. 76% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the dark outline reads as near-black or grey rather than a tinted dark tone of the rock. The result is a somewhat sticker-like, thinner and flatter silhouette than the Beodeul props, which have 5-6 steps per material and tinted outlines. Slightly shallow overall, so it fails.
